cases.given: A fresh supported SQLite database with no incident_categories or it_services tables.
cases.then: Initialization succeeds and both parent tables exist with zero records.

cases.given: The initialized incident_categories table is empty.
cases.when: Distinct category names are inserted with and without descriptions, including a name outside the project statement examples; inserts with NULL names and duplicate names are attempted, then valid categories are retrieved by their IDs.
cases.then: Valid categories receive stable integer primary-key IDs and retain their names and optional or NULL descriptions; valid new names require no schema change. NULL-name and duplicate-name inserts are rejected without adding rows.

cases.given: The initialized it_services table is empty.
cases.when: Services are inserted with each of low, medium, high and critical business criticality and with optional descriptions omitted or supplied; inserts with NULL names, duplicate names, NULL or omitted criticality, and unsupported criticality are attempted; valid services are retrieved by their IDs.
cases.then: Valid services receive stable integer primary-key IDs and retain names, descriptions and their one supplied allowed criticality. Each invalid insert is rejected without adding a row, and no criticality is supplied by default.

cases.given: A supported existing account database contains users and other stored data but does not yet have the parent tables.
cases.when: The standalone initializer runs, category and service records are subsequently added, and initialization runs again.
cases.then: The first run creates both parent tables empty without changing existing accounts or other data; the second run preserves the category and service identities, values, users and other data, and valid parent-table records remain retrievable.
